title: Public Speaking
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Un líder no solo tiene buenas ideas, sabe cómo venderlas. Ahora tienes el vocabulario para dominar el escenario y cautivar a cualquier audiencia.

parts.visual:
Para liderar, debes saber hablar frente a multitudes. 

1. Captivate the audience (Cautivar a la audiencia): 
- Atraer y mantener completamente la atención del público. 
Ej: A great speaker knows how to CAPTIVATE THE AUDIENCE from the first second. 

2. Cut to the chase (Ir al grano): 
- Dejar de dar rodeos y llegar al punto importante. 
Ej: We only have 5 minutes, so let me CUT TO THE CHASE. 

3. Anecdote (Anécdota): 
- Una historia corta y personal usada para ilustrar un punto. 
Ej: He started his speech with a funny ANECDOTE about his first job.
parts.audio: Welcome to Public Speaking and Presentations. To lead, you must know how to speak to crowds. Number 1: Captivate the audience. To attract and hold the interest and attention of the public completely. For example: A great speaker knows how to CAPTIVATE THE AUDIENCE from the first second. Number 2: Cut to the chase. To stop talking about unimportant details and get to the main point immediately. For example: We only have 5 minutes, so let me CUT TO THE CHASE. Number 3: Anecdote. A short, interesting, and often personal story about a real incident, used to illustrate a point. For example: He started his speech with a funny ANECDOTE about his first job.

parts.visual:
4. Rhetorical question (Pregunta retórica): 
- Una pregunta que se hace para crear efecto, no para recibir una respuesta. 
Ej: Asking 'Are we ready for the future?' is a powerful RHETORICAL QUESTION. 

5. Rule of three (Regla de tres): 
- El principio de que las ideas presentadas en grupos de tres son más memorables (ej: Blood, sweat, and tears). 
Ej: Steve Jobs always used the RULE OF THREE in his presentations. 

6. Handout (Folleto / Material impreso): 
- Papeles entregados a la audiencia con información extra. 
Ej: I have prepared a HANDOUT with the financial graphs. 

7. Q&A session (Sesión de preguntas y respuestas): 
- El momento al final donde el público hace preguntas. 
Ej: We will have a 10-minute Q&A SESSION at the end.
parts.audio: Number 4: Rhetorical question. A question asked in order to create a dramatic effect or to make a point, rather than to get an answer. For example: Asking 'Are we ready for the future?' is a powerful RHETORICAL QUESTION. Number 5: Rule of three. The writing principle that suggests that things presented in threes are funnier, more satisfying, and more memorable. Like 'Blood, sweat, and tears'. For example: Steve Jobs always used the RULE OF THREE in his presentations. Number 6: Handout. A printed document provided to the audience containing extra information. For example: I have prepared a HANDOUT with the financial graphs. Finally, Number 7: Q&A session. Question and Answer session at the end of a talk. For example: We will have a 10-minute Q&A SESSION at the end.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término de presentaciones correcto.

questions.question: The CEO's speech was so boring that half the room fell asleep. He completely failed to ____ the audience. (Cautivar).
questions.explanation: Captivate the audience = cautivar a la audiencia.

questions.question: I know you have a lot of slides, but we are running out of time. Please just cut to the ____. (Ir al grano).
questions.explanation: Cut to the chase = ir al grano.

questions.question: Instead of showing boring statistics, she started with a personal ____ about her grandfather. (Anécdota).
When he asked the crowd, 'Do you want to work forever?', he didn't want them to answer. It was a ____ question.
Humans remember patterns. Grouping your ideas like 'Veni, vidi, vici' utilizes the Rule of ____.
questions.explanation: Rule of three = la regla de tres (grupos de tres elementos).

questions.question: Don't write everything on the slides. I will give you a printed ____ with all the technical details later. (Folleto/Material impreso).
questions.explanation: Handout = material impreso que se reparte.

questions.question: If you have any doubts, please save them for the ____ session at the end of my speech. (Preguntas y respuestas).
When you lose your train of thought and forget what you were going to say, you 'go ____'. (Quedarse en blanco).
questions.explanation: Go blank = quedarse en blanco (olvidar todo).

questions.question: To speak without preparation, making it up as you go, is to ____ it. (Improvisar).
questions.explanation: Wing it = improvisar, hacerlo sobre la marcha.

questions.question: A short, memorable phrase used in marketing or politics (like 'Just Do It') is a ____. (Eslogan / Frase gancho).
questions.explanation: Catchphrase (o slogan) = frase célebre o eslogan.

questions.question: A very brief, extracted audio clip of someone speaking, used by the news media, is a sound ____.
questions.explanation: Sound bite = clip de audio corto e impactante para las noticias.

questions.question: Speaking louder so the people in the back can hear you is called ____ your voice. (Proyectar).
questions.explanation: Project your voice = proyectar la voz.

questions.question: If you speak too fast or quietly, you might ____ your words, making them impossible to understand. (Murmurar/Masticar las palabras).
questions.explanation: Mumble = murmurar o hablar entre dientes.

questions.question: The visual aids you show on screen (PowerPoint, Keynote) are generally called your ____. (Diapositivas).
A presenter who reads word-for-word from their notes without looking at the audience lacks ____ contact. (Contacto visual).
The physical position and movements of your body while speaking is your ____ language. (Lenguaje corporal).
To give a short overview or summary of what you are going to talk about is to give an ____. (Resumen/Esquema).
The device that slowly scrolls the text of a speech so the speaker can read it while looking at the camera is a ____. (Teleprónter).
If the microphone suddenly makes a loud, high-pitched ringing noise, that is audio ____. (Acople/Retroalimentación).
questions.explanation: Audio feedback = acople (el ruido agudo del micrófono).

questions.question: To finish your presentation by repeating the most important message is to summarize your key ____. (Conclusiones principales).
questions.explanation: Key takeaways = los puntos clave que el público debe llevarse a casa.

questions.question: ____ the audience. (Cautivar con C)
Cut to the ____. (Ir al grano con C)
A funny ____. (Anécdota con A)
A ____ question. (Pregunta retórica con R)
The Rule of ____. (Regla de tres con T)
A printed ____. (Folleto informativo con H)
A 10-minute ____ session. (Preguntas y respuestas con Q)
My mind went ____. (Me quedé en blanco con B)
I didn't practice, I'll just ____ it. (Improvisar con W)
Summarize your key ____. (Puntos clave/conclusiones con T)
